topic: The Mystery of Pi in Block Collisions
target_audience: Undergraduate students in Physics or Computer Science

sections.title: The Setup: Elastic Collisions
lecture_lines: Two blocks collide on a frictionless surface.
Momentum and energy are conserved in elastic collisions.
Consider a massive block hitting a small one.
animations: Show initial velocity vectors vM and vm.
Animate elastic collision: blocks bounce with new velocities.
Display and highlight conservation equation p_i = p_f (#FFFF00).

sections.title: Visualizing the Collision Count
lecture_lines: Add a wall behind the smaller block.
The block bounces between the wall and big block.
A counter tracks the total number of collisions.
animations: Animate M hitting m, then m hitting.
Increment and display counter (#FFFFFF) on each collision.

sections.title: The Mathematical Bridge
lecture_lines: Increasing mass ratios change the collision count.
The count converges to digits of Pi.
This links simple physics to transcendental numbers.
animations: Display collision formula M/m ratio using. Label as R (#00FFFF).
Show R=100 results in 31 collisions involving.
Morph R into Pi value approximation 3.14.

sections.title: Geometric Interpretation
lecture_lines: Phase space visualizes collision states as trajectories.
Reflections happen within a V-shaped mirror wedge.
The trajectory angle depends on the mass ratio.
Reflections count the slope to escape the wedge.
Geometry interprets the physical collision count.
animations: Draw a V-shaped wedge using white lines (#FFFFFF).
Show a point bouncing inside the wedge.
Show trajectory reflecting off the wedge walls.

sections.title: Conclusion and Intuition
lecture_lines: Discrete collisions map to digits of Pi.
Laws of physics constrain the system.
Simple interactions compute complex mathematical truths.
animations: Display summation of total collisions as Pi digits.
Flash final Pi result in #FFFF00 to conclude.
